changes.year1_quote: On November 30, 2020, a joint announcement by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, and the OCC was released and included a statement that the administrator of LIBOR has announced it will consult on its intention to cease the publication of the one week and two month USD LIBOR settings immediately following the LIBOR publication on December 31, 2021, and the remaining USD LIBOR settings immediately following the LIBOR publications on June 30, 2023.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: On March 5, 2021, the FCA confirmed that all LIBOR settings will either cease to be provided by any administrator or no longer be representative immediately after December 31, 2021 for the 1-week and 2-month US dollar settings and immediately after June 30, 2023 for all remaining US dollar settings.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 Item 7A disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk and cessation timeline: discontinuation of the 1-week and 2-month USD LIBOR settings after December 31, 2021 and the remaining USD LIBOR settings after June 30, 2023. The language is updated from a proposed consultation to the FCA's confirmed outcome, but this does not change the disclosed economic risk.

changes.year1_quote: Synovus holds instruments that may be impacted by the discontinuance of LIBOR including floating rate obligations, loans, deposits, derivatives and hedges, and other financial instruments but is not able to currently predict the associated financial impacts of the transition to an alternative reference rate.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Synovus holds instruments that may be impacted by the discontinuance of LIBOR, which include floating rate obligations, loans, deposits, derivatives and hedges, and other financial instruments... As of December 31, 2021, the Company had approximately $14 billion in loans tied to LIBOR that mature after June 30, 2023. Remediation activities are underway to modify or transition existing exposures to alternate index rates or to convert the rate under existing fallback language.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk—Synovus's exposure to LIBOR-linked instruments and the need to manage the financial effects of LIBOR discontinuance—remains expressly disclosed. Year-2 provides more specific exposure data and remediation actions; although it says the Company does not expect a material financial impact, it does not eliminate or materially downgrade the exposure itself.
